name: h2oGPT (H2O.ai Stateful Open-Source RAG + LLM inference)
notable_features: The 'Stateful Open-Source RAG + LLM inference system' - a full private document-QA stack, not an inference kernel. Reads PDFs, Excel, Word, images, video frames, YouTube, audio, code, text and Markdown
Pluggable vector stores: Chroma, Weaviate or in-memory FAISS, with selectable embedding models (instructor-large, all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
HYDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) for retrieval using the LLM's own hypothetical answers as the query
Semantic chunking, which the README flags as requiring a GPU
Attention sinks for arbitrarily long generation on LLaMA-2, Mistral, MPT, Pythia and Falcon
Two inference backends in one project - HuggingFace models and LLaMA.cpp GGML on GPU; HF, LLaMA.cpp and GPT4ALL on CPU. This dual path is the niche interest
Supports AutoGPTQ at 4-bit/8-bit and LORA adapters
Gradio UI or CLI with streaming, plus a wide set of side models (LLaVA and other vision models, Stable Diffusion, Whisper STT, Microsoft Speech T5 TTS, Flux)
Claims 80 tokens/s summarization with a 13B LLaMA2 model (vendor claim, no methodology given)
Claims over 1000 unit and integration tests taking over 24 GPU-hours as a quality signal
hardware_caveats: ARCHIVED. The GitHub API reports archived=true on h2oai/h2ogpt as of 2026-10-03. Last push 2025-10-09; last release 0.2.1 from 2024-06-04, i.e. releases stopped over two years ago while 1188 open issues accumulated

The repo points at a commercial successor: the README's first substantive link is 'Try Enterprise Version for Free' at h2ogpte.genai.h2o.ai. The open-source line was retired into the enterprise product rather than superseded by another OSS runtime

NAME COLLISION - do not confuse this with the 'H2O' kNN-LLM paper by Shi et al. (kNN-LM: Generalization through Memorization, arXiv:1911.00172). Unrelated projects, unrelated authors, wildly different reception. This is H2O.ai, the Wisconsin company behind H2O-3
The RAG side is where the GPU requirement hides: the README explicitly marks semantic chunking as needing a GPU, so the 'CPU support' claim covers LLM inference but not the full pipeline
Its dual HF-plus-llama.cpp design means it inherits both projects' format and quality problems, including that GGML-era and HF-era checkpoints of the same model give different answers
11954 stars and an archived flag is the whole story: this is the fate of OSS stacks that outgrow their serving engine
best_for: Studying what a complete private-RAG product needs beyond an inference engine, and how much of that is vector-store plumbing rather than model serving
Reading the HYDE and semantic-chunking implementations as concrete code
Historical: it is the clearest public example of the OSS-RAG-stack-to-enterprise-product transition
avoid_for: Anything new - the repo is archived and releases stopped in June 2024
Serving: it is a RAG application, not an engine. If you want the LLM serving part use [[llama-cpp]] or [[vllm]]
Retrieval research: use ColBERT / PLAID (see [[niche-colbert]]) or a maintained vector database instead of a wrapper around Chroma and FAISS
